newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Compromise unlikely in HKG shipping talks - Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Compromise unlikely in HKG shipping talks - Taiwan.

text.p: Taiwan and Hong Kong will resume shipping talks in a bid to overcome key sovereignty hurdles that threaten to disrupt bilateral routes after the British colony reverts to China in July, officials said on Monday.

Taiwan officials cautioned, however, that they were unlikely to make concessions on the thorny issue of what flags the sides' ships should fly while sailing the routes, reducing prospects of a breakthrough at the talks on Saturday .
Taiwan's quasi-official Straits Exchange Foundation said a second round of talks with the Hong Kong Shipowners' Association would open on May 24 in Taipei. The first was held in Hong Kong.
"We will continue to discuss the flag-flying issue," a foundation spokeswoman said.
Talks on how to continue crucial direct shipping services after Hong Kong's July 1 handover to China ended without a deal on May 2 with the sides deadlocked on the flag issue.

Beijing, which regards Nationalist Taiwan as a renegade province, objects to any ship entering Hong Kong harbour flying the flag of the exiled Republic of China, which took refuge on Taiwan after its 1949 civil war defeat to the communists.
Beijing has proposed the sides each use their respective flower flags -- Hong Kong's tropical bauhinia flag and Taiwan's winter plum blossom flag.
A senior official of the Taiwan cabinet's policymaking Mainland Affairs Council, Shi Hwei-you, said Taipei was unlikely to give in on the controversial flag issue.

"We can't possibly agree to the plum blossom flag," Shi told state radio. "It's not a national flag, but a trap set by the Chinese communists to brand us as a local area, similar to that of Hong Kong."
Taipei has proposed the sides simply lower their flags while entering each other's harbour, but this was rejected by Beijing on the grounds that only pirates sail without flags.
Shi said flying the plum blossom flag or the Olympic flag were gimmicks to undermine Taiwan's government by portraying it, like Hong Kong, as a region not a sovereign state.
Taiwan has accepted the five-ring Olympic flag and the name "Chinese Taipei" when attending international sports events.
Shi called on Beijing to "stop using gimmicks" and to talk with Taipei with a "practical and pragmatic" attitude.
Anxious Taiwan shippers urged Taipei and Beijing to keep politics out of the talks as time was running out.
"The Taiwan-Hong Kong shipping negotiations shouldn't be politicised and should be resolved in a practical manner," said Taiwan Shipping Association president Lin Shen-san.
